summary: Iteration 5 verified the new multi-user Emergent Google auth layer and end-to-end data isolation, plus full regression of iterations 1-4. Backend: 62 pytest tests / 62 passed (0 failed). New coverage: (1) test_auth_gating.py [25 tests] — every protected endpoint (GET /council,/settings,/sessions,/sessions/{id},/sessions/{id}/export,/openrouter/models,/auth/me and POST /settings,/sessions,/message,/respond,/notes,/conclude,/review,/synthesize,/tts,/stt) returns 401 with no cookie AND no Bearer; bogus Bearer + bogus cookie both 401; POST /api/auth/session with invalid session_id → 401; GET /api/ = 200 public; POST /api/auth/logout is a no-op public 200; valid Bearer + valid cookie both authenticate GET /auth/me and /council. (2) test_isolation.py [10 tests] — two users A & B seeded in Mongo; A creates a session and sets provider_keys.openai='sk-test-fake-...'; A lists exactly her session, B lists 0; B's GET/POST(message)/DELETE/GET(export) on A's session all return 404 (and A's session still exists after B's DELETE attempt confirming per-owner filter, not per-id no-op); GET /settings for A shows providers_configured.openai=true, for B shows false; GET /council reflects same; raw key text 'sk-test-fake-isolation-KEY-DO-NOT-LEAK-98765' NEVER appears in any response body (POST /settings, GET /settings, GET /council) for either user; response body has no 'provider_keys' or 'openrouter_key' fields. Regression (all as authed user A): council roster (5 members + scribe + providers[] + openrouter_configured + any_provider_configured), sessions CRUD, message length cap 422 @8001, synth question cap 422 @4001, TTS text cap 422 @8001, STT 415 on non-audio & non-415 on audio/mpeg, PDF export returns application/pdf + %PDF magic + >500 bytes, review 'two members must speak' 400 guard, synthesize graceful 400/502 without keys, respond without OpenRouter key graceful 400/502, TTS returns audio_base64 (Emergent key), rate-limit burst still yields 429 with 'rate limit' detail. Frontend: unauthenticated GET / redirects to /login; Login page renders google-login-btn 'Sign in with Google'; clicking navigates to https://auth.emergentagent.com/oauth/?redirect=<origin>/. Authed dashboard (via readable session_token cookie seeded in Mongo): home renders user-avatar ('C'), user-name ('Council FE Tester'), open-settings-btn ('Configure'), logout-btn, 5 council cards, 'Add subscription or OpenRouter key' amber notice; logout-btn clears session cookie and returns to /login (401 interceptor confirms API layer wired).
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE /api/sessions/{sid} always returns {ok:true} even when the filter {id,owner} matched nothing (i.e. non-owner or unknown id). Not a security bug (data untouched, verified by test_b_cannot_delete_a_session), but the response is misleading — consider raising 404 when delete_one.deleted_count==0 so clients cannot infer 'success' from a cross-tenant delete.

get_current_user() sets a ContextVar `_current_user_id`, and get_settings()/get_provider_key()/get_openrouter_key() read from it. This is used from *sync-appearing* helpers called inside async request handlers — safe in FastAPI because each request runs in its own task with its own context. However if these helpers are ever awaited from a background task or gather() *not* triggered by a request path, they will silently fall back to global scope. Consider passing user_id explicitly.

/api/auth/session sets cookie samesite=none + secure=True + httponly=True — correct for the cross-site Emergent → app redirect. But allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True is technically forbidden by the CORS spec (Chromium & Safari refuse Access-Control-Allow-Origin:'*' with credentials). Middleware echoes the actual Origin so it works in practice, but consider constraining to explicit origins for defence in depth.

user_sessions.expires_at is stored as an ISO string; get_current_user parses it back and compares to now(UTC). Works, but a proper datetime BSON field would let Mongo TTL-index expire tokens automatically (`db.user_sessions.createIndex({expires_at:1},{expireAfterSeconds:0})`).
auth_session upserts users by email — good idempotency. However it stores session_token verbatim in Mongo. Consider hashing (SHA-256) at rest, so a DB dump doesn't yield working bearer tokens.

Frontend logout() awaits apiLogout() then hard-navigates to /login. On the /api/auth/logout path, the backend clears cookie only if it exists in the request; but since the browser sends cookies with credentials:true and Axios withCredentials:true this is fine. Just noting: if the response Set-Cookie doesn't include SameSite=None/Secure, Safari may keep the stale cookie — verify in production.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (unauth redirect + login btn + authed home dashboard + logout all verified)

test_credentials: Seeded per-test via conftest.py — two users A & B inserted into `test_database.users` + `test_database.user_sessions` per /app/auth_testing.md pattern; auth via `Authorization: Bearer <session_token>`. Frontend authed UI test used a separate short-lived session_token cookie (readable, secure, samesite=None). EMERGENT_LLM_KEY used for TTS (verified 200). No OpenRouter/provider real keys — graceful 400/502 paths verified.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral. All seeded users A/B and their user_sessions/sessions/settings docs are teardown-deleted by the session-scoped conftest fixture (delete by exact user_id — no broad regex to avoid xdist worker races). Verified post-run: 0 residual test users, 0 residual test_session_* tokens, 0 residual TEST_-prefixed sessions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth: seed users via pymongo — see /app/backend/tests/conftest.py (fixtures `seeded_users`, `s`, `sb`, `token_a`, `token_b`). Do NOT restore the broad-regex 'safety-net' cleanup in conftest — it races between pytest-xdist workers (each seeds its own users; broad delete_many from one worker wipes the other's live users mid-test). If a test needs a raw requests session (not from the `s` fixture), add `Authorization: Bearer <token_a>` explicitly (see test_expensive_endpoint_rate_limit_burst). The `s` fixture in conftest.py deliberately does NOT set Content-Type: application/json globally, because requests needs to set multipart/form-data itself for file uploads (STT tests). Total: 62 tests / 62 passed in ~21s (xdist -n 2 --dist loadscope, per pytest.ini).
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. During test authoring, three initial failure modes were fixed within the test harness (not app code): (1) STT tests 422'd because the shared `s` session had Content-Type:application/json which overrode the multipart boundary that `files=` needs — removed the default JSON content-type from the fixture; (2) test_providers.py originally had a same-named local `s` fixture that took precedence over conftest's authed session — removed it; (3) inter-worker race where one xdist worker's teardown wiped the OTHER worker's live seeded users via a broad email-regex delete — replaced with exact-user_id delete.
